slides.stem: If $y = \frac{1}{2}x + 3$ and $3x - 2y = 10$, what is the value of $x$?

slides.intro: Substitute, then distribute the $-2$ to both terms.
slides.trapWhy: Every wrong choice here is a distribution slip. The $-2$ must hit both the $\frac{1}{2}x$ and the $3$.

slides.title: Distribute to every term
slides.body:
When a substitution puts parentheses behind a negative, the sign multiplies through everything inside — the fraction term and the constant.

The dropped constant is one of the most common algebra points lost on this test.

slides.title: When you miss one like this, Seva tells you why.
